title.value: Towards Non-saturating Recurrent Units for Modelling Long-term Dependencies
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Towards Non-saturating Recurrent Units for Modelling Long-term Dependencies

analysis.description: The paper addresses the challenge of modeling long-term dependencies in recurrent neural networks by introducing a new architecture called Non-saturating Recurrent Unit (NRU). The aim is to alleviate the vanishing gradient problem common in traditional RNNs by avoiding saturating activation functions and gates. The NRU relies on a memory mechanism with a non-saturating approach, using ReLU activations to improve gradient flow and enable better learning of long-term dependencies. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of NRU across various synthetic and real-world tasks, showing superior performance in comparison to other existing architectures.

type.justification: The study involves experiments comparing the proposed NRU unit with existing architectures on synthetic and real-world tasks.
type.quote: In this section, we compare the performance of NRU networks with several other RNN architectures in three synthetic tasks (5 including variants) and two real tasks.

name.justification: The paper primarily focuses on addressing challenges within recurrent neural networks (RNNs) by introducing a new unit.
name.quote: Vanishing and exploding gradients remain a core challenge in the training of recurrent neural networks.

name.justification: The paper talks extensively about the vanishing gradient problem which is critical to training neural networks via gradient descent.
name.quote: Vanishing gradients prevent the network from learning long-term dependencies (Hochreiter 1991; Bengio, Simard, and Frasconi 1994) and arise when the network dynamics have attractors necessary to store bits of information over the long term (Bengio, Simard, and Frasconi 1994).

name.justification: NRU is described as a memory-augmented architecture that addresses long-term dependencies using memory in new ways.
name.quote: Other related lines of work which aim to model long-term dependencies in RNNs are Memory Augmented Neural Networks (MANNs) (Graves, Wayne, and Danihelka 2014; Graves et al. 2016; Gülçehre et al. 2018; Gülçehre, Chandar, and Bengio 2017).

name.justification: The paper introduces this as the primary research contribution to address long-term dependency issues.
name.quote: We propose a new recurrent architecture (Non-saturating Recurrent Unit; NRU) that relies on a memory mechanism but forgoes both saturating activation functions and saturating gates, in order to further alleviate vanishing gradients.
